Shared actor state feeds cooperative following and train formation.
Human following remains the default within-lane behavior before lateral action.
SDV-Train state and signals become multilane inputs.
Two-step signaling provides the NSDV lane-change execution shell.
The same signaling shell receives SDV pair and train changes.
NSDV trajectories feed mixed-fleet and lane-efficiency outputs.
SDV and train trajectories feed share, valley and dedicated-lane outputs.
P1 following behavior contributes to load-speed curves.
Short train gaps contribute to the capacity mechanism.
LCP sensitivity reopens the NSDV lane-choice parameters.
Speed-limit sensitivity reopens discrete speed and timing choices.
